title: Fusobacterium nucleatum infection is prevalent in human colorectal carcinoma
central_claims: Fusobacterium nucleatum is enriched in colorectal cancer relative to matched normal tissue, with an invasive isolate and association with nodal metastasis.

source_manifest.title: Replication Study: Fusobacterium nucleatum infection is prevalent in human colorectal carcinoma.
source_manifest.finding: Replication had many nondetects and smaller effects; combined meta-analysis favored enrichment but assay specificity confounded inference.

source_manifest.title: Association of Fusobacterium nucleatum infection with colorectal cancer in Chinese patients.
source_manifest.finding: Independent 101-patient Chinese cohort found enrichment in 88 tumors, confirmed by FISH and linked to nodal metastasis.

source_manifest.title: Fusobacterium nucleatum potentiates intestinal tumorigenesis and modulates the tumor-immune microenvironment.
source_manifest.finding: Fusobacterium increased mouse intestinal tumor multiplicity and altered immune microenvironment, extending the association mechanistically.
